docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
SQLify is a new kind of database which does not store any data.

At the core of SQLify is the capability to query various remote data sources using SQL. To do so, we have added new capabilities to SQL. We call this superset SQLETL.

There are no tables in an SQLify database. All the data is accessed in real-time when a query is performed.

SQLify speaks the PostgreSQL protocol: you can connect to it with psql, BI tools or any PostgreSQL driver.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
No need for installation if using uv:

$ uvx sqlify

But if you are planning to use it frequently:

$ uv tool install sqlify

docs.title: Starting the server
docs.text:
$ SQLIFY_SYSTEM_PWD=password sqlify

The server listens on 127.0.0.1:55432 by default. Options: --listen-addr, --port, --ssl-cert, --ssl-key, --max-clients.

Databases, roles and their configuration are stored in a sqlify.db file in the current directory.

docs.title: First queries
docs.text:
The server exposes a system user and a system database for administrative purposes.

$ psql -h localhost -U system -p 55432 system

Query a URL directly:

SELECT * FROM "http://example.com/path" WHERE "?param" = 'value';

Create a database and a role (see databases and roles):

CREATE DATABASE mydb;
CREATE ROLE alice PASSWORD 'secret';
GRANT ON mydb TO alice;

Then, connected to mydb, store credentials and create views:

CREATE CREDENTIALS ON "https://api.example.com" TOKEN 'my-token';
CREATE VIEW users AS SELECT * FROM "https://api.example.com/users";
SELECT * FROM users;

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text: Credentials can be centrally managed instead of being provided for each query. They apply to every URL starting with the given URL (see URL matching).

docs.title: Username/password
docs.text:
Create a set of HTTP auth credentials for an endpoint.

CREATE CREDENTIALS ON "http://example.com/path" AUTH 'username:password'
CREATE CREDENTIALS ON "postgresql://myserver.com" AUTH 'username:password'
CREATE CREDENTIALS ON "s3:///bucket" AUTH 'aws_key:aws_secret'

docs.title: Bearer token
docs.text:
A "Bearer" token that will be provided through the Authorization header

CREATE CREDENTIALS ON "http://example.com/path" TOKEN 'token'

docs.title: Header
docs.text:
A value that will be added as header

CREATE CREDENTIALS ON "http://example.com/path" HEADER 'X-Header=value'

docs.title: Query parameter
docs.text:
A value that will be added as query parameter

CREATE CREDENTIALS ON "http://example.com/path" PARAM 'name=value'

docs.title: Remote
docs.text:
Credentials can be fetched from another service when a query is executed. SQLify sends a POST request to the given URL with the db and role form fields. The service must respond with a JSON object providing the credentials type (auth, token, header or param) and value.

CREATE CREDENTIALS ON "http://example.com/path" REMOTE 'https://vault.example.com/credentials'

If the service does not respond with a 200 status code, no credentials are used.

docs.title: Naming credentials rules
docs.text:
You can name rules:

CREATE CREDENTIALS cred1 ON "http://example.com/path" TOKEN 'token'

Then use the named rule:

SELECT * FROM "http://cred1@example.com/path/to/rest/endpoint"

When a URL contains a username and password (http://user:pass@example.com), stored credentials are not used.

docs.title: Listing credentials
docs.text:
Credential values are never displayed.

SHOW CREDENTIALS

docs.title: Removing a credentials rule
docs.text:
DROP CREDENTIALS ON "http://example.com/path"
DROP CREDENTIALS cred1

docs.title: Querying across databases
docs.text:
You can join tables from different databases by prefixing the table name with the database name. The current role must have access to both databases.

SELECT * FROM "my table in current db" t1 JOIN "other database"."table in other db" t2 ON ...

You can query any data source as if it was from another database. This is useful to re-use credentials from another db.

SELECT * FROM "other database"."https://api.example.com/users"

docs.title: Setting up a database schema
docs.text:
SQLify provides a way to define a dynamic schema for your database using the CREATE SCHEMA statement.

CREATE SCHEMA WITH
    TABLES AS (SELECT ...)
    COLUMNS AS (SELECT ...)
    ROWS AS (SELECT ...)

TABLES AS defines a select statement that returns a list of tables. It is mandatory to return at least a "name" column.

COLUMNS AS is optional. It defines a select statement that returns a list of columns. It is mandatory to return at least a "name" column.

ROWS AS defines a select statement that returns the rows for the table.

Select statements from COLUMNS AS and ROWS AS can access data from the current table using $TABLE[column_name].

Example with Notion:

CREATE SCHEMA WITH
    TABLES AS (
        SELECT id, title->0->plain_text AS name
        FROM "POST https://api.notion.com/v1/search?JSON#results"
        WHERE "?filter.value" = 'database' AND "?filter.property" = 'object'
    )
    COLUMNS AS (
        WITH props AS (
            SELECT unnest(properties)
            FROM "https://api.notion.com/v1/databases/$TABLE[id]"
        )
        SELECT value->id AS id, key AS name FROM props
    )
    ROWS AS (
        SELECT id, expand(properties)
        FROM "POST https://api.notion.com/v1/databases/$TABLE[id]/query#results"
    )

Query parameters can be forwarded to the underlying query by using the "+" parameter:

SELECT id, expand(properties)
FROM "POST https://api.notion.com/v1/databases/$TABLE[id]/query?+#results"

The list of tables and columns is fetched when the schema is created. Fetch it again with:

REFRESH SCHEMA

To inspect the schema:

SHOW SCHEMA;
SHOW TABLES;
SHOW TABLE mytable;  -- columns of a table

Tables and views are also listed in information_schema, so PostgreSQL clients can browse them.

To remove the schema:

DROP SCHEMA

docs.title: Databases and roles
docs.text: Databases and roles are managed from the system database, connected as the system user (database admins can also manage access to their databases, see below). The system user's password is set with the SQLIFY_SYSTEM_PWD environment variable when starting the server. Without it, the system user cannot log in.

docs.title: Databases
docs.text:
CREATE DATABASE mydb;
DROP DATABASE mydb;
SHOW DATABASES;

When connected as another role, SHOW DATABASES lists the databases the role has access to.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
CREATE ROLE alice PASSWORD 'secret';
ALTER ROLE alice PASSWORD 'other';

A role without a password cannot log in. To disable a role, remove its password:

ALTER ROLE alice PASSWORD NULL;

Dropping a role removes its grants. The databases are kept unless WITH DATABASES is used, in which case the databases the role administers are dropped too:

DROP ROLE alice;
DROP ROLE alice WITH DATABASES;

docs.title: Grants
docs.text:
A role can only connect to the databases it has been granted access to.

GRANT ON mydb TO alice;
REVOKE ON mydb FROM alice;

By default, access is read-only: the role can run queries but cannot change the database (views, credentials, schema...). To allow it, grant admin access:

GRANT ADMIN ON mydb TO alice;

A database can be exposed to a role under another name. Here, alice connects to analytics, which is the mydb database:

GRANT ON mydb TO alice AS analytics;

Granting again on the same database replaces the previous grant.

docs.title: Delegating access management
docs.text:
Admins of a database can also grant and revoke access to it, including admin access, without going through the system user. They can do so while connected to any database they have access to, and can refer to the database by its alias:

-- connected as alice, admin of mydb
GRANT ON mydb TO bob;
GRANT ADMIN ON mydb TO carol;
REVOKE ON mydb FROM bob;

The role must already exist: only the system user can create roles. Admins cannot grant or revoke access to databases they do not administer.

docs.title: Acting as another role
docs.text:
Connected as the system user, you can run queries as another role:

SET ROLE alice

docs.title: Data sources
docs.text: These statements configure how data sources are accessed in the current database. They are stored with the database and apply to every query.

docs.title: Aliases
docs.text:
An alias gives a table name to a URI.

CREATE ALIAS users AS "https://api.example.com/users#data";
SELECT * FROM users;

SHOW ALIASES;
DROP ALIAS users;

docs.title: Schemes
docs.text:
A scheme defines a custom URI scheme. $PATH is replaced with everything after ://.

CREATE SCHEME gh AS "https://api.github.com/$PATH";
SELECT * FROM "gh://repos/sqlifyme/sqlify/issues";

SHOW SCHEMES;
DROP SCHEME gh;

docs.title: Headers
docs.text:
Add an HTTP header to all requests whose URL starts with the given URL. Several headers can be added to the same URL.

CREATE HEADER ON "https://api.notion.com" AS 'Notion-Version: 2022-06-28';

SHOW HEADERS;
DROP HEADER "https://api.notion.com";  -- removes all headers for this URL

To send a secret in a header, use credentials instead: their values are never displayed.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
Paginated HTTP APIs can be fetched in full. SQLify keeps requesting pages and merges the rows until there is no next page.

CREATE PAGINATION ON "<url>" AS <param>=<location>(<name>)
  • param: the query parameter used to request the next page
  • location: where to find the value of the next page in the response, either header or body
  • name: the header name, or a JSONPath in the response body
-- next page value in the "next_cursor" field of the JSON body, sent as ?cursor=...
CREATE PAGINATION ON "https://api.example.com" AS cursor=body(next_cursor);

-- next page value in the X-Next-Page response header, sent as ?page=...
CREATE PAGINATION ON "https://other.example.com" AS page=header(X-Next-Page);

SHOW PAGINATIONS;
DROP PAGINATION "https://api.example.com";

docs.title: URL matching
docs.text: Credentials, headers and pagination rules apply to every URL starting with the rule's URL. When several rules match, the longest one wins. * can be used as a path segment: "https://example.com/*/items".

docs.title: SQLETL
docs.text:
SQLify queries are written in SQLETL, a superset of SQL provided by the sqletl library. Everything that works in sqletl works in SQLify.

The full SQLETL reference is available at sqlifyme.github.io/sqletl.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The main idea of SQLETL is that a table name can be a URI. The data is fetched, parsed and transformed when the query runs:

SELECT u.name, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM "https://api.example.com/users#data" u
JOIN "s3:///my-bucket/orders.parquet" o ON o.user_id = u.id
GROUP BY u.name
  • Sources: HTTP(S) (GET and POST), files, S3, FTP, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Google Sheets (protocols)
  • Formats: JSON, CSV, XLSX, Parquet, SQLite, detected automatically or forced with scheme+format:// (data formats)
  • Request parameters from SQL: WHERE "?param" = 'value' is sent to the source as a request parameter, and URL templates such as "https://example.com/users/{id}" are filled from WHERE "?id" = 1 (HTTP)
  • Nested data: select rows with a JSONPath in the URI fragment (#data.items), access fields with -> / ->>, flatten with EXPAND() and UNNEST()
  • SQL processing: joins, GROUP BY, window functions, ORDER BY, LIMIT, CTEs

Some SQL features are not supported yet, see the limitations.

docs.title: What SQLify adds
docs.text:
SQLify runs SQLETL queries as a PostgreSQL compatible server and adds statements to manage what is stored in a database:

  • Credentials so that secrets are not written in queries
  • Aliases, schemes, headers and pagination for data sources
  • Views and schemas
  • Databases and roles

Use EXPLAIN to see how a query will be executed without running it:

EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM "https://example.com/api/items" WHERE "?q" = 'a' OR "?q" = 'b'

Note

In SQLify, file:// URIs are relative to a folder dedicated to each database (user_files/<database> next to the server's sqlify.db file) and cannot reach files outside of it.

docs.title: Views
docs.text: SQL views are possible in SQLify

docs.title: Managing views
docs.text:
CREATE VIEW myview AS SELECT * FROM "http://example.com";
SELECT * FROM myview;

To list views and show the query of a view:

SHOW VIEWS;
SHOW VIEW myview;

To remove a view;

DROP VIEW myview

docs.title: Materialized views
docs.text:
Materialized views are also possible. SQLify caches the data when the view is created. Refreshing is done manually:

CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW myview AS SELECT * FROM "http://example.com";
SELECT * FROM myview;
REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW myview;
